status: development comparison overlays; independent admission not performed

groups.label: Copy RNA into a cDNA reporter

members.explanation: RNA-templated DNA synthesis is combined with stochastic AzNTP termination; the copied product has an intentionally blocked reactive end.
RNA-templated DNA synthesis yields cap-reaching and premature cDNA outcomes; downstream cap trapping treats those outcomes differently.

groups.summary: Both selected operations copy RNA into DNA by reverse transcription. Their primer architecture, termination behavior and desired products differ; this grouping asserts only that scoped copying mechanism.

evidence.basis: direct visual diagram and explanatory text review
archived candidate operations, mechanisms and source corrections inspected; cited primary passages not independently reopened for this comparison

limitations: Not a statement that the entire operations are equivalent or interchangeable.
Shared reverse transcription does not establish lineage or transfer of conditions.
CAGE archived separate output States describe molecular outcomes, not proven separate reaction fractions; this grouping does not endorse that old state partition.

groups.label: Select RNA-origin reporters through terminal features

members.explanation: Differential end treatment makes originally cyclic-phosphate-bearing RNA dual-adapter-ligatable while susceptible other ends remain blocked; the entire sequence is needed to explain the selection.
Copying, biotinylation, RNase protection and capture retain cDNA associated with a capped RNA end. Both successful and rejected molecular outcomes are included; the short branch fails capture.

groups.summary: Both recover a reporter population determined by an original RNA-end feature. cP-RNA selects through chemical protection and ligatability; CAGE selects cap-associated, 5-prime-complete cDNA through a hybrid/capture route.

evidence.basis: direct visual diagram and explanatory text review

evidence.locator: cp-rna-seq.candidate.operations[o_cip,o_periodate,o_pnk,o_ligate]; cage-seq.candidate.operations[op_rt through op_purify, both outcome branches]
evidence.basis: archived candidate operations, mechanisms and source corrections inspected; cited primary passages not independently reopened for this comparison

limitations: Different end features, selected populations, substrates and mechanisms; this is a comparison of purpose, not a reusable interchangeable module.
Archived cP and CAGE split molecular fates into separate State records. They must not be rendered as independently aliquoted samples or new physical separations.
Neither the original cyclic phosphate nor RNA cap should be assigned as a chemical modification on the recovered DNA reporter.

groups.label: Connect reporter sequence to library handles

members.explanation: Chemical adapter joining creates a triazole-linked cDNA template; subsequent PCR depends on polymerase read-through of that junction.
End conversion establishes an adapter-ligatable RNA substrate, then ligation and RT-PCR make a DNA library from dual-adapter-bearing RNA.
The source-level barcoding/P7 block is resolved by the archived primary correction as PCR on ligated DNA probes. Its library is probe-derived, not an RNA-to-cDNA product.

groups.summary: These connected source blocks give the reporter the handles needed for library amplification, using different substrates and interfaces: click-linked cDNA, enzymatically adapter-ligated RNA, and primer-incorporated handles on a DNA probe reporter.

evidence.basis: direct visual diagram and explanatory text review
archived candidate operations, mechanisms and source corrections inspected; cited primary passages not independently reopened for this comparison

limitations: Broad shared purpose only; neither a shared reaction nor an assertion of comparable yields.
RASL catalogue capture/ligation ordering differs from its primary protocol; selection of op_index avoids endorsing the disputed earlier order.
ClickSeq polymerase read-through must remain an interface requirement; a joined DNA-looking glyph alone does not establish amplifiability.
